pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with a CHECK on the three values. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
src/index.js item() appends ' — high' or ' — low' and nothing for normal. 'AC-2' asserts the exact list items.
The WHERE priority = ? ORDER BY id query is covered by 'AC-3' for high, low and normal, including id order.
The unfiltered query orders by id. 'AC-4' asserts the full list in order.
nav() renders all four filters with the current one as <strong>. 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav HTML for all four views.
searchParams.has('priority') combined with a Set check returns 400. 'AC-6' covers High, urgent, empty and __proto__, and asserts no <li> in the body.
The empty message comes from a COUNT query. 'AC-7' covers no-match for high, low and normal, and 'No items yet.' in all four views when the table is empty.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. 'AC-8' asserts it. The checker regex now allows a query, and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers that.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent and decisions. It adds nothing the spec doesn't call for beyond the traffic-checker query allowance, which the PR discloses and AC-8 requires.
All 8 acceptance items are met, and all four state-table rows have tests in the 'states' describe block. The spec was added in the same commit as the code, with the go dated 2026-10-12.

The tests assert exact rendered output and would fail on wrong code. Nothing was deleted or loosened. The traffic fake app now keys on path plus query. I could not run `npm test` because vitest isn't installed here, so CI has to cover that.
The README describes the `?priority=` filter. CLAUDE.md and the README on routes.json stay accurate.
The priority value is validated against a Set and bound as a parameter. Titles are HTML-escaped. The 400 path and the empty-state logic are correct.
No injection path: the query is parameterised, the label values come from a CHECK-constrained column, and the filter value is validated before use.
The diff touches only a server-rendered minimal HTML page with no styling or UI files, and the PR says there are no screenshots.
There is no browser flow to demonstrate in this session; the PR says there is no browser.
The title is under 72 characters. The claims about the migration, the tests, the traffic checker and the README match the diff.
